dish: neighbourhood-bar burgers and cheap drinks on the patio
w: Thornton Park's 80-plus-year neighbourhood bar — one of downtown's longest-lived establishments, reopened under the same name in 2017 by The Lodge/The Woods owners; Orlando Weekly: the area's 'cheapest and friendliest' with a prime people-watching patio.

dish: seasonal Italian from the on-site Primo Garden
w: Two-time James Beard winner Melissa Kelly's farm-to-table Italian in the JW Marriott Grande Lakes (since 2003, redesigned 2021) — MICHELIN Guide Florida listed since the 2022 inaugural edition; produce, honey and eggs from its own garden.

dish: chef Tony Lopez's seasonal fine dining (grouper with pecan butter)
w: Dr. Phillips fine-dining fixture for 30+ years — chef Tony Lopez's locally sourced menu; Orlando Weekly essential Dr. Phillips pick, reviewed and Magical Dining-featured by Scott Joseph.

dish: baked kibbeh, mezze
address: 7732 W Sand Lake Rd, Orlando, FL 32819
w: Restaurant Row's upscale Lebanese dining room — baked kibbeh and mezze; Orlando Weekly's Dr. Phillips guide, Scott Joseph listing.

dish: robatayaki skewers and sushi
w: Dellagio's Japanese robata grill and sushi bar (from Gainesville) — five-time Florida Trend Golden Spoon winner (2015-19); reviewed by Orlando Weekly ('Mister Robata') and Scott Joseph.

dish: family-style Sichuan classics (mapo tofu, dry-fried dishes)
address: 1035 N Orlando Ave #105, Winter Park, FL 32789
w: MICHELIN Guide Florida Recommended (2024-26) — Winter Park's polished Sichuan dining room with a large family-style menu of layered, bold classics; Tasty Chomps inside look.

dish: smoked fish dip, fish & chips, shrimp 'n' grits
address: 761 N Orange Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
w: Former Orlando Weekly Best Seafood Restaurant winner — dockside-casual counter with a fresh-fish case (Orlando Weekly essential Winter Park; Scott Joseph review).

dish: tapas (croquetas, paella) by chef Diego Solano
address: 110 S Orlando Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
w: Winter Park's Spanish tapas bar — chef Diego Solano's Barcelona-style small plates and cocktails (Orlando Weekly essential Winter Park; Winter Park Magazine 'Bite of Barcelona').

dish: sashimi, robata skewers, Japanese-fusion small plates
address: 525 S Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
w: Park Avenue sushi and robata bar — Orlando Weekly: 'stellar sashimi and robata offerings'; Scott Joseph review; Visit Orlando listing.

dish: Dominican-remix sushi rolls
w: Dominican-Japanese sushi hideaway — Gastro Obscura video feature and stop on the Experience Kissimmee × Atlas Obscura Latin Culinary Trail.

dish: Venezuelan arepas and patacones from Paraguaná
address: 2381 N Orange Blossom Trl, Kissimmee, FL 34744
w: Venezuelan kitchen on the Gastro Obscura × Experience Kissimmee Latin Culinary Trail.

dish: Mexican tacos and antojitos
w: Mexican stop on the Gastro Obscura × Experience Kissimmee Latin Culinary Trail.

dish: Venezuelan llanero grill plates
w: Venezuelan grill on the Gastro Obscura × Experience Kissimmee Latin Culinary Trail.

dish: space-themed cocktails with launch-pad views
w: Rooftop bar-restaurant atop the Courtyard Titusville Kennedy Space Center — the closest hotel rooftop to Launch Complexes 39A/39B, open to non-guests (cover on launch nights); Space Coast Living readers' Best Romantic Dinner; WFTV + News 6 coverage.

dish: fresh seafood on the upper deck as cruise ships sail out
address: 610 Glen Cheek Dr, Cape Canaveral, FL 32920
w: Port Canaveral channel-side seafood house — the Port's webcam spot for watching cruise sail-aways and rocket launches from its tiki sun deck (FOX 35 'Beach Bites'; AAA).

dish: globally inspired, locally sourced tasting-style plates
w: Historic downtown DeLand's destination restaurant built by multi-time James Beard nominee Hari Pulapaka (now chef-owner Tom Brandt) — 2025 DiRōNA Award, 2025 Wine Spectator Award of Excellence (Scott Joseph; DiRōNA).

dish: honey chicken, Korean fried chicken sandwich, egg rolls
address: Asia, Disney's Animal Kingdom, Bay Lake, FL 32830
w: Asia's walk-up counter beside the Yak & Yeti restaurant (Landry's-run, no mobile order) — TouringPlans review ranks it in WDW's top half of 111 quick-service spots; KennyThePirate review.

dish: mac and cheese bowls
address: Discovery Island, Disney's Animal Kingdom, Bay Lake, FL 32830
w: Discovery Island kiosk famous for its mac-and-cheese variations (TouringPlans 'comfort food haven'; Disney Food Blog).

dish: burgers and nuggets in a dig-site HQ (closed)
address: DinoLand U.S.A., Disney's Animal Kingdom, Bay Lake, FL 32830
w: DinoLand's paleontology-camp counter — permanently closed 2 Feb 2026 for the Pueblo Esperanza land construction (Disney Food Blog; WDWInfo; BlogMickey 'final review').

dish: lamb and chicken kebabs, gyros, hummus
address: The Lost Continent, Universal Islands of Adventure, Orlando, FL 32819
w: Lost Continent counter for kebabs and gyros — TouringPlans' 'This Not That' Universal dining pick; ranked in Islands.com's IOA restaurants list.

dish: giant cinnamon rolls, weekend brunch among antiques
w: Ivanhoe Village's 30-plus-year 'Orlando Classic' (Scott Joseph) — an antique shop turned cafe-bar, named for the owners' white shepherd; Orlando Weekly readers' #2 Ivanhoe Village restaurant 2025; Food Network's $40 a Day stop; Tasty Chomps snapshots.

dish: breakfast plates and daily quiche under a wall of salt-and-pepper shakers
w: College Park's breakfast-and-lunch diner (since the 1990s) named for its salt-and-pepper-shaker collection — Scott Joseph 'bona fide Orlando Classic' and Foodster Best Breakfast 2017; Orlando Weekly Edgewater essential + Best of Orlando 2026 entry.

dish: cooked-to-order subs and shakes from the original milkshake machine
w: Paul Gabriel's family-run College Park sub shop (1958) — one of Orlando's oldest restaurants, still with its original milkshake machine and dining furniture (News 6 'last remaining iconic restaurants of Orlando' 2023; Orlando Weekly Edgewater essential).

dish: Mediterranean-inspired prime cuts and seafood
w: Dr. Phillips' Mediterranean-leaning modern steakhouse — Orlando Weekly readers' Best Sand Lake/Dr. Phillips Restaurant 2026 (ahead of DOMU and Seito); its group took over Restaurant Row's Vines Grille as Vines by H in 2025 (Central Florida Lifestyle).
